Subject: Your next rainy-day ridge line — meet the Stormline Shell
Preview: 420 g, 20k/20k rated, built for days when the weather doesn't cooperate.
Body: You already know that a wet jacket at mile eight is a different problem than a wet jacket at the trailhead. The Northbay Stormline Shell (NB-JKT-07) is built around that reality.

Here's what the specs mean in practice:

• 20,000 mm waterproof rating — enough to hold up through sustained, heavy rain, not just a passing shower.
• 20,000 g/m²/24hr breathability — the 3-layer laminate moves moisture out while keeping rain from getting in, so you're not choosing between wet from outside or wet from sweat.
• 420 g total weight — light enough to carry without noticing it, substantial enough to anchor a layering system in real conditions.
• 3-layer construction — the face fabric, membrane, and backer are bonded together, which eliminates the interior liner that traps moisture in cheaper shells.

A fair note on limits: the Stormline is a hardshell designed for rain and wind. It's not insulated, so it works best as part of a layering system. It's not sized or padded for technical climbing or high-altitude mountaineering — it's a trail and alpine approach jacket.

If you're planning trips where the forecast is genuinely uncertain and you need a shell that earns its place in the pack, the Stormline is worth a look.
